NC: 2024:KHC:10690  CRL.RP No. 897 of 2021  THIS CRL.RP IS FILED UNDER SECTION 397 R/W 401 OF CR.PC PRAYING TO SET-ASIDE THE ORDER DATED 12.03.2020 PASSED IN SPL.C.C.NO.376/2014 PENDING ON THE FILE OF LXXVIII (CCH-79) ADDITIONAL CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS COURT AND SPECIAL JUDGE, P.C. ACT, BENGALURU VIDE ANNEXURE-A AND ETC.
 THIS PETITION COMING ON FOR ADMISSION THIS DAY,

THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER
This matter is listed for admission today.

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1.
2.
The present petition is filed challenging the order dated 12.03.2020 passed in Spl.C.C.No.376/2014.

The case of the prosecution is that though FIR was not registered against the present petitioner at the first instance, during the course of investigation in view of the Investigating Officer collected the certificate issued by accused No.4 on 12.03.2003 and 17.03.2003 respectively,
along with accused No.3 case has been registered against accused No.4/petitioner herein.

Inclusion of this petitioner is based upon the certificates which have been referred above and hence the Trial Court rejected the discharge application in coming to the conclusion that prima facie there NC:
2024:KHC:10690 are materials to proceed against the petitioner and hence they are no entitled for discharge.
Being aggrieved by the said order, the present petition is filed.
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the Special Court committed an error in rejecting the application filed under Section 227 of Cr.P.C.

The learned counsel would contend that the charge-sheet filed against accused No.1 has been set aside by this Court in W.P.No.54107/2014 and as such, the charge-sheet filed against the petitioner/accused No.4 cannot be continued.

Hence,
continuing the criminal proceedings against accused No.4 is illegal and improper and the same is liable to be set aside as per the law laid down by this Court in Crl.P.No.101228/2012 dated 20.04.2022.

The learned counsel would contend that CID police without conducting proper investigation have filed the charge- sheet against the petitioner by including this petitioner with Dr. S. Malini vs The State Of Karnataka on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65321833/
2 other accused.

sentences.text:
The learned counsel would contend that the departmental enquiry has also been initiated against the petitioner and the petitioner has been exonerated in the departmental enquiry,
but it is not on technical ground, but it is on merits as there was no evidence against the petitioner to drive home the charge.
The learned counsel contends that when NC: 2024:KHC:10690 the petitioner has been exonerated in the departmental enquiry, continuing the proceedings against this petitioner is erroneous.

The learned counsel would also contend that from the reported judgment of this Court passed in W.P.No.19700/2018 dated 27.07.2021, it is clear that if the allegations in the departmental enquiry could not be proved on merit and the person is held to be innocent, the criminal proceedings on the said facts cannot be permitted to be continued on the underlying principles of criminal trial needing higher standing of proof.
Hence, continuing criminal proceedings against the petitioner is illegal.

4. The learned counsel would also contend that the charge-sheet is filed after four years and at the first instance, case was registered against accused No.1 and only while filing the charge-sheet, the name of this petitioner is included after four years of the period of limitation and also not sought for any extension of period of limitation as contemplated under Section 473 of Cr.P.C.
The learned counsel would contend that FIR was registered on 30.07.2010 and CID police have filed the charge- sheet on 21.08.2014.
The learned counsel contends that the complaint filed by the complainant is purely civil in nature.
The non-selection of the post of Scientific Assistant is confirmed by the Karnataka Administrative Tribunal ('KAT' for short).
The NC: 2024:KHC:10690 complainant has not challenged the order passed by the KAT against the complainant.
Hence, the order passed by the KAT has become final and the baseless complaint filed by the complainant is not maintainable under law.
The CID police have included the name of the petitioner in the charge-sheet only on the ground of the statement made by the co-accused No.1 Dr. B.M.Mohan.
It is well settled law that on the basis of statement of co-accused, the police cannot include the name of unconnected person in the charge-sheet.

The sanction order produced before the Trial Court said to have been issued by the Government is not supported by any other materials on record to establish that actually the Government has taken any decision and thereafter the Government has directed the Under Secretary to communicate the said order to the accused.

5. Per contra, the learned High Court Government Pleader submits that specific charge is made against the petitioner that this petitioner was working as Assistant Director and this petitioner conspired with accused Nos.1 and 3 and issued certificate in favour of accused No.2 stating that accused No.2 was working with us on honorary basis from October 2002 till December 2002 and from December 2002 to till date, he is working as Research Assistant in the project entitled "Nuero NC: 2024:KHC:10690 Psychological Methods of Interrogation of Suspects" and the said certificate is fake and on the basis of the said false certificate, accused No.1 gave second false certificate in favour of accused No.2.

Hence, the Trial Court comes to the conclusion that the petitioner has not disputed the issuance of certificate dated 17.03.2003 and the Investigating Officer collecting the same, invoked the offence punishable under Sections 166, 167, 197, 198, 120B read with 37 of IPC and under Section 13(1)(d) read with Section 13(2) of Prevention of corruption Act and hence no grounds are made out.

sentences.text: Having heard the respective learned counsel and having considered the charges leveled against the petitioner that this petitioner colluding with accused Nos.1 and 3 gave false certificate stating that accused No.2 worked for a period of six months even though no such work was done and based on the certificate issued by this petitioner, accused No.1 issued a certificate in favour of accused No.2 and specific charge is levelled against the petitioner herein.

The learned counsel for the petitioner would contend that the order passed by the Trial Court is against the order passed by this Court in W.P.No.54107/2014, wherein this Court made an observation with regard to, it becomes necessary to consider the purport NC: 2024:KHC:10690 and impact of the complete exoneration on its merits in departmental enquiry qua the petitioner and the proceedings pending before the criminal Court impugned herein.
The issue need not detain this Court for long as it is no longer res integra.

The same is not applicable to the facts of the case on hand, since specific allegation made against the petitioner is that this petitioner had indulged in creation of false certificate and based on the false certificate, accused No.1 also gave second false certificate in favour of accused No.2.
It is also a specific allegation that this petitioner in connivance with accused Nos.1 and 3 issued the said false certificate.

7. The Trial Court having considered the material on record comes to the conclusion that this petitioner has not been arraigned as accused only at the instance of voluntary statement of accused No.1, but during the course of investigation, the names of accused Nos.3 and 4 are included in the final report since the Investigating Officer did collect the certificate issued by accused Nos.3 and 4 on 12.03.2003 and 17.03.2003 respectively.

When the certificate is issued by the petitioner on 17.03.2003, based on material evidence, the Investigating Officer did include this petitioner in the final report and the same is observed by the Trial Court and whether the NC: 2024:KHC:10690 petitioner has issued the certificate on 17.03.2003 or not

, is a matter of trial and rightly comes to the conclusion that the petitioner is not entitled for discharge under Section 227 of Cr.P.C., when serious allegation is made against the petitioner in issuance of false certificate and conspiracy is also alleged against the petitioner.
No doubt, there is a delay in including the petitioner as an accused.
The case was registered at the first instance against accused No.1 and other accused and the matter was investigated by the CID and hence there was a delay in filing the final report.

The offences invoked against the petitioner is for the offence punishable under Section 166, 167, 197, 198, 120B read with 37 of IPC and under Section 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) of Prevention of Corruption Act.

Hence, the very contention that filing of charge-sheet belatedly after four years is hit by limitation,
cannot be accepted considering the penal provisions invoked against the petitioner.

Hence, I do not find any ground in the petition to set aside the order passed by the Trial Court in rejecting the application filed under Section 227 of Cr.P.C.
NC: 2024:KHC:10690 8.

In view of the discussions made above, I pass the following:
ORDER
The petition is dismissed.
